sam-altman.quote: The only solution I can come up with is to orient towards sharing the technology with people broadly, and for no one to have the ring.

sam-altman.claim: Altman says safety must be gotten right and urgently requires a society-wide response beyond model alignment.

sam-altman.claim: Altman argues compute is the limiting factor for AI's benefits and urges building far more infrastructure.

source.title: Abundant Intelligence

source.title: Abundant Intelligence

sam-altman.quote: We are past the event horizon; the takeoff has started. Humanity is close to building digital superintelligence, and at least so far it’s much less weird than it seems like it should be.
sam-altman.claim: Altman says the takeoff has started and humanity is close to building digital superintelligence.

source.title: The Gentle Singularity

sam-altman.quote: In the 2030s, intelligence and energy—ideas, and the ability to make ideas happen—are going to become wildly abundant.
sam-altman.claim: Altman predicts intelligence and energy will become wildly abundant in the 2030s.

source.title: The Gentle Singularity

sam-altman.quote: The least-likely part of the work is behind us; the scientific insights that got us to systems like GPT-4 and o3 were hard-won, but will take us very far.
sam-altman.claim: Altman says the scientific insights behind current systems like GPT-4 and o3 will take AI very far.

source.title: The Gentle Singularity

sam-altman.quote: It appears that you can spend arbitrary amounts of money and get continuous and predictable gains; the scaling laws that predict this are accurate over many orders of magnitude.
sam-altman.claim: Altman says spending more on compute and data yields continuous, predictable intelligence gains per scaling laws.

source.title: Three Observations

sam-altman.quote: Many of us expect to need to give people more control over the technology than we have historically, including open-sourcing more, and accept that there is a balance between safety and individual empowerment that will require trade-offs.
sam-altman.claim: Altman expects to give people more control over AI, including open-sourcing more, while accepting safety trade-offs.

source.title: Three Observations

sam-altman.quote: the economic growth in front of us looks astonishing, and we can now imagine a world where we cure all diseases, have much more time to enjoy with our families, and can fully realize our creative potential.
sam-altman.claim: Altman foresees astonishing economic growth and a world where all diseases are cured.

source.title: Three Observations

sam-altman.quote: We continue to believe that the best way to make an AI system safe is by iteratively and gradually releasing it into the world, giving society time to adapt and co-evolve with the technology
sam-altman.claim: Altman says iterative, gradual release into the world is the best way to make AI safe.

source.title: Reflections

sam-altman.quote: We are now confident we know how to build AGI as we have traditionally understood it.
sam-altman.claim: Altman says OpenAI is confident it knows how to build AGI.

source.title: Reflections

sam-altman.quote: Superintelligent tools could massively accelerate scientific discovery and innovation well beyond what we are capable of doing on our own, and in turn massively increase abundance and prosperity.
sam-altman.claim: Altman says superintelligent tools could massively increase abundance and prosperity.

source.title: Reflections

sam-altman.quote: I expect that by the end of this decade, and possibly somewhat sooner than that, we will have quite capable systems that we look at and say, "Wow, that's really remarkable."
sam-altman.claim: Expects remarkably capable systems by the end of the decade or sooner.
